decisions.reason: Vocative comma is natural English; the Korean period after 형 is vocative punctuation, not a hard beat.
Present-tense “Are you hurt?” matches the current-state check of 안 다치셨어요.
Past “stood there and watched” is the natural English accusation for their completed failure to help; Korean present is accusatory vividness.
“Things were a little complicated back there” is spoken English for 그때 상황이 좀 그랬어요; BASE’s “the situation…then” is stiffer.
Tighter rhetorical “Who had forced those…” and standing-belief “had always thought” read as natural narration without changing the giving/receiving claim.
SOL drops the source image 뒤통수가 얼얼했다, flattening it to generic “The betrayal stung.”
Leaner, more natural wording; “in his name” still covers 명의로 잡힌 without the heavier “registered under.”
“Could never” carries the absolute force of 도저히, which BASE’s “couldn’t” underplays.
SOL omits 부릅뜬 눈으로; BASE’s “with wide-open eyes” is calqued onto “glared.”
decisions.replacement: Im Changsoo glared at one person’s back, his eyes wide.

decisions.reason: 원흉 is the prime culprit/root cause; SOL’s “cause” weakens it.
“Who Taekyung was” is the natural English for 정체가 뭔지, not the stiffer “what Taekyung’s identity was.”
“A single C-rank Hunter in the world” keeps the 세상 어디에도 emphasis; SOL’s trim is not an improvement.
BASE’s “fugitive criminal” is tautological; SOL turns 부정 등록자 from a person-category into the action “falsify.”
decisions.replacement: *Why is he hiding his identity? Is he a fugitive? Or someone with a fraudulent registration? The moment we get out of this Gate, I’ll dig up every last thing about him.*

decisions.reason: Restores the omitted beat of 은밀히 복수심을 불태우고 있던 그때였다 that BASE cut.
Restores the source SFX 휙, which BASE dropped.
Reunites the turn-and-narrow-eyes action with the predator-gaze beat after the restored 휙.
“I wasn’t” agrees with “You were just cursing me”; 아닌데요 denies the accusation, not a separate “didn’t.”
“Says it all” lands 사이즈 나오는데; “this whole time” naturalizes 아까부터, unlike “since earlier.”
대격변 시대 needs “era”; SOL drops 시대.
“Must respond” fits a remembered precept better than spoken “have to deal with it.”
Keeps the denial aligned with “were cursing”: “I really wasn’t.”
“Why can’t there be mind-reading?” is complete spoken English for 관심법이 왜 없어.
“Either way…wasn’t” is more spoken for 어쨌든 and stays consistent with the were/wasn’t denial.
“You’ve got one coming too” is the tighter threat idiom for 너도 한 대 맞아, and “you were” matches the accusation.
Bonk matches the comic 꿀밤 register; Thwack over-weights 빡 into a heavier strike.
꿀밤 is a knuckle rap, not a light flick; SOL also captures 그것도 with “no less” in cleaner syntax.
Spoken Taekyung cadence; “Feels just like hitting Hyuk Mujin” is less translationese than “The feel is exactly like when I hit.”
“Had no idea” is stronger, more natural English for 누군지는 모르겠지만.
“Never ends” and “how much farther is it” are more natural spoken English for 끝도 없네 / 얼마나 남았어.
Split punchline gives the 안 나오지 outburst better comic rhythm without losing the cause.
Past perfect fits the retrospective: they already hadn’t needed to step in.
진짜 is “really,” not “actually.”
펄펄 날아다녔다 is vigorous combat energy, not literal flying; “tearing through them” naturalizes the idiom.
“Slowed toward the end” is tighter without changing 느려지는.
Korean is 레이드 속도; SOL replaces raid pace with generic “they were moving faster.”
계속해서 is continuous getting-stronger, not SOL’s “still.”
Keeps the interior thought; SOL shifts it to narration and inserts an unstated “Taekyung.”
꿀밤 is a forehead hit, not a “blow”; BASE doesn’t overstate the knuckle rap.
후우 has no ellipsis; the following line already marks the deep sigh.
어떡해 here is fussing “oh no,” not a literal “what do we do?”
너희는 나가기만 하면 has “you” leaving; SOL’s “we get out” changes the subject.
체면 is dignity/face; SOL’s generic “humiliated” blurs it into the earlier 굴욕.
“Haven’t even finished paying off my car” is the natural English for 할부 안 끝났는데.
“Who’ll take me” is the idiomatic reading of 어디에서 받아 주나.
Cuts the 이유는…덕분이다 cleft into direct English without losing support, hunger, or treatment.
BASE adds “getting away with it”; SOL drops 상동 길드 이름으로 for a call merely “from” the Guild.
decisions.replacement: “You think it ends with getting fired? Just wait. Wherever you go, I’ll make sure to place a call in Sangdong Guild’s name. You know this field is small, right?”

decisions.reason: Leading with the expression change is more natural English word order.
“Only your hyung when it suits you” is the idiomatic bite of 너 좋을 때만 형이냐.
줄을 대다 is patronage; SOL’s “side with” loses the hitch-your-wagon meaning.
“Every last one of them” fits the angry 모두 better than flat “every one.”
또 belongs on 돌아볼지, not on raising his voice; SOL then drops 언제 … 모르기.
decisions.replacement: If he raised his voice, there was no telling when Jin Taekyung might turn around again.

decisions.reason: 내가 어쩌다가…… trails off; SOL completes it with unsupported “like this.”
Fragment plus “How pathetic” captures 꼴이라니 better than BASE’s explained “forehead flick.”
응? is “Okay?,” not BASE’s “Please?”
“I mean it. I really will” preserves the doubled 진짜 / 진짜로 that BASE flattens.
Echoes the groveling “anything” promise just made; same 다 한다고 pickup.
뿌리치려던 is shaking the hand off, not “pull away”; cleaner sentence besides.
Puts the argument-distance cause before the result; same facts, better flow.
SOL drops 뒤태; the point is her figure from behind.
그의 눈에 비친 is how Taekyung looked to Changsoo; SOL states “was a monster” as fact.
송송이라는 여자 is the distancing “a woman named Song Song”; SOL deletes it.
눈치채고 말고 할 것도 없다 is outright obviousness, not SOL’s milder “wasn’t exactly difficult.”
English idiom is wringing a chicken’s neck; “move so freely” is a clean 손을 쓸 수 없을.
“Their Guild Master” and condensed E-rank tank are clearer; 쥐약 as close-combat weakness is adequate.
SOL drops 약간; the bother is specifically slight.
사람을 왜 못 믿어 is “people,” not narrowed “us”; “only this close” matches 이 정도 사이.
“Eat only from his hand” keeps the 먹이/길들여진 domestication image; BASE’s “scraps” is extra.
긴장된 기색 is nervousness/tension, not milder “unease.”
가능성 있어 보이기는 is seeming/looking possible, not “sound.”
More natural spoken hedging for 설마 내가 생각하는 그거 and 사람 죽이는 거면 나는 좀.
“Just say you’d do anything” matches the immediately prior grovel and 다 한다고.
Elided “I’d like to” and “put through a humiliation” are more idiomatic for 안겨 줘야지.
“On your side, oppa” is natural address; 오빠 편 doesn’t need the stiff “oppa’s side.”
SOL’s 잘해 as “Do it right” is right, but it drops 조금이라도.
decisions.replacement: “Do it right. You know what happens if anyone hesitates this time or holds back even a little, right?”

decisions.reason: “Who he had dared to cross” carries 겁도 없이 누굴 건드렸는지; BASE’s “toes” misses the daring.
Clear pronoun after Taekyung in the prior line; no need to repeat the name.
대전사 is Great Warrior, not merely Warrior; first on-page title should keep 대.
Anaphoric “Great Warrior” follows the 대전사 title just established.
“In one stroke” restores 한 번에, which BASE omitted.
보스 존이잖아 is spoken “It’s the Boss Zone,” not the stiffer “This is.”
경쾌하기 그지없었다 is extremely light, not a “than ever” comparison.
The sky-splitting sentence is kept in the merged next paragraph; not an omission.
Merges the spear-tip sound into 1st-person “my spear” and keeps 대전사 as Great Warrior.
System line is Lv.70 미노타우로스 대전사; Great Warrior is required for 대전사.
역시 마지막은 큰 거 한 방이지 is “the last one [is] one big hit,” not SOL’s “nothing beats.”
BASE’s “dead … corpse” is tautological; SOL drops 사체 entirely.
decisions.replacement: He looked back and forth between the boss monster’s corpse and me.

decisions.reason: 끝장냈으니 is “finished off,” the right English phrasal verb.
BASE’s “The fact that” is calqued 것도; SOL’s luck framing is good but adds an unstated “someone.”
decisions.replacement: Lucky that I had lived in a goshiwon.[^1] Lucky that a capsule had been discarded in front of it.

decisions.reason: “Too dumbfounded to speak” covers both 기가 차서 and 말도 안 나오는구먼; “speechless” only covers the latter.
“Been on a raid with me, looked stunned” is natural; the following line already is the 한마디.
이 정도일 줄은 몰랐 is didn’t know/realize, not “didn’t expect.”
지금 알면 됐죠 is “knowing now is enough”; SOL’s “Well, now you know” drops 됐죠.
지금은 아니고, 나중에 is “Not now. Later”; SOL’s “Just” is extra.
“Putting on” can imply a fake smile; 미소를 지으며 is simply wearing his most charming smile.
Ellipsis with no extra space matches 그냥, 그냥 and house style.
언니가 너무 예쁘셔서 is a present reason; SOL’s past “thought she was” changes it.
붙어 있던 as clustered, plus “blurting out whatever came to mind,” matches 아무 말 대잔치 panic better than “spouting nonsense.”
뭐야, 이것들 is “What’s with these guys,” not “what’s wrong with.”
방해되니까 is getting in the way; SOL’s merely “standing between” weakens the interference.
한마디에 is a single remark; 쫙 갈라졌다 is split apart, stronger than “parted.”
대답했다 is answered; SOL replaces it with unsupported “stood.”
집에 돈 많잖아 is household wealth; “Your family’s rich” naturalizes BASE’s calqued “money at home.”
수거하고 가자 is two beats, collect then let’s go, not a purpose clause.
“Flashed … a bright smile” is the natural English for 활짝 웃어 보였다.
것 같은데 is seeming; “You seemed to eat meat” is closer than “I thought you ate.”
Deadpan 까인 거 맞지 should stay short; SOL adds “just” and a heavier tag.
